Project Documentation - Architecture Overview

The system follows a microservices architecture with the following components:

1. API Gateway (Node.js): Handles all incoming requests, performs authentication and rate limiting.
2. User Service (Python/FastAPI): Manages user accounts, profiles, and authentication.
3. Order Service (Go): Processes orders, manages inventory, and handles payments.
4. Notification Service (Node.js): Sends emails, SMS, and push notifications.
5. Analytics Service (Python): Collects and processes usage data for reporting.

All services communicate via gRPC internally and expose REST APIs externally. Data is stored in PostgreSQL for relational data and Redis for caching. Message queues use RabbitMQ for asynchronous processing.

The deployment pipeline uses Docker containers orchestrated by Kubernetes. CI/CD is managed through GitHub Actions with automated testing and deployment.

Monitoring is handled by Prometheus and Grafana for metrics, and the ELK stack for logging. Alerting is configured through PagerDuty.

Security measures include:
- JWT-based authentication with refresh tokens
- Rate limiting on all API endpoints
- Input validation and sanitization
- HTTPS for all external communications
- Regular security audits and penetration testing

The system is designed to be horizontally scalable with auto-scaling configured based on CPU and memory utilization. Database replication ensures high availability with automatic failover.

Development follows the Git Flow branching strategy with feature branches, develop branch, and main branch. Code reviews are mandatory for all pull requests.

The technology stack is chosen based on team expertise and community support. Regular dependency updates are performed to address security vulnerabilities.

Documentation is maintained in the docs directory and includes API references, architecture diagrams, and deployment guides.

Company Handbook - Employee Guidelines

Welcome to the team! This handbook covers essential information about our company policies and procedures.

Work Hours:
- Standard work hours are Monday through Friday, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM
- Flexible scheduling is available with manager approval
- Remote work is permitted up to 3 days per week

Communication:
- Primary communication tool is Slack
- Email is used for formal communications and external contacts
- Meetings should have a clear agenda and desired outcomes
- Asynchronous communication is preferred for non-urgent matters

Time Off:
- 15 days of paid vacation per year
- 10 sick days per year
- 12 public holidays
- Additional leave for parental and bereavement

Benefits:
- Comprehensive health insurance
- 401(k) matching up to 6%
- Annual learning budget of $2,000
- Wellness program with gym membership discount

Performance Reviews:
- Conducted quarterly
- Focus on goals, achievements, and growth areas
- 360-degree feedback from peers and stakeholders

Code of Conduct:
- Treat all colleagues with respect and professionalism
- Maintain confidentiality of company and client information
- Report any concerns to HR or the ethics hotline
- Zero tolerance for harassment or discrimination

Technology Policy:
- Use company-provided equipment for work
- Follow security protocols for data handling
- Do not install unauthorized software
- Report any security incidents immediately

Career Development:
- Internal mobility is encouraged
- Mentorship programs are available
- Skills training and certifications are supported
- Regular career conversations with managers

We value collaboration, innovation, and continuous learning. If you have questions about any policy, please contact HR.

Technical Specification - API Design Document

Version: 2.1.0
Last Updated: 2026-01-15

1. Overview
This document describes the REST API for the platform. All endpoints follow RESTful conventions and return JSON responses.

2. Authentication
All API requests must include a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Tokens are obtained via the /auth/login endpoint and expire after 24 hours.

3. Endpoints

3.1 User Management
GET /api/v1/users - List users (paginated)
POST /api/v1/users - Create user
GET /api/v1/users/{id} - Get user by ID
PUT /api/v1/users/{id} - Update user
DELETE /api/v1/users/{id} - Delete user

3.2 Authentication
POST /api/v1/auth/login - User login
POST /api/v1/auth/logout - User logout
POST /api/v1/auth/refresh - Refresh token

3.3 Content Management
GET /api/v1/content - List content
POST /api/v1/content - Create content
GET /api/v1/content/{id} - Get content
PUT /api/v1/content/{id} - Update content
DELETE /api/v1/content/{id} - Delete content

4. Response Format
All responses include a status field indicating success or error. Successful responses include a data field with the requested information. Error responses include an error field with a code and message.

5. Error Codes
200 - Success
201 - Created
400 - Bad Request
401 - Unauthorized
403 - Forbidden
404 - Not Found
429 - Too Many Requests
500 - Internal Server Error

6. Rate Limiting
API requests are limited to 1000 requests per hour per token. Exceeding this limit results in a 429 error with a Retry-After header.

7. Pagination
List endpoints support pagination via page and limit query parameters. Default page size is 20, maximum is 100.

8. Versioning
The API uses URL-based versioning (/api/v1/). Breaking changes will increment the version number.

9. Security
- All communications over HTTPS
- Input validation on all parameters
- SQL injection prevention via parameterized queries
- XSS prevention via output encoding
- CSRF protection for state-changing operations

10. Rate Limits and Quotas
Free tier: 100 requests/hour
Pro tier: 1000 requests/hour
Enterprise: Custom limits

Meeting Minutes - Q1 2026 Planning Session

Date: January 15, 2026
Attendees: Product Manager, Engineering Lead, Design Lead, QA Lead, Marketing Lead

Agenda:
1. Review Q4 2025 results
2. Set Q1 2026 objectives
3. Resource allocation
4. Risk assessment

Q4 2025 Review:
- Revenue exceeded target by 12%
- User growth was 8% below target due to seasonal slowdown
- Product launch of Feature X was successful with 95% adoption
- Customer satisfaction score improved from 4.2 to 4.5

Q1 2026 Objectives:
1. Launch Feature Y by end of February
2. Increase user acquisition by 15%
3. Reduce customer churn by 5%
4. Complete migration to new infrastructure
5. Launch mobile app beta

Resource Allocation:
- Engineering: 60% on Feature Y, 20% on infrastructure, 20% on bugs
- Design: 50% on Feature Y, 30% on mobile app, 20% on UX improvements
- Marketing: 40% on user acquisition, 30% on retention, 30% on brand
- QA: 50% on Feature Y testing, 30% on regression, 20% on automation

Risks Identified:
1. Feature Y scope may be too large for Q1 - Mitigation: prioritize core functionality
2. Infrastructure migration could cause downtime - Mitigation: blue-green deployment
3. Hiring for senior engineers is slow - Mitigation: use contractors for critical roles
4. Competitive landscape is changing - Mitigation: maintain agile development

Action Items:
- Engineering Lead: finalize Feature Y technical design by Jan 22
- Product Manager: create detailed project plan by Jan 20
- Design Lead: complete Feature Y mockups by Jan 25
- Marketing Lead: launch Q1 campaign by Feb 1
- QA Lead: set up testing environment by Jan 22

Next meeting: January 22, 2026

All action items will be tracked in the project management tool.
